newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures end mixed.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle cattle futures ended mixed, capping a thinly-traded, abbreviated session with distant live cattle and spot January feeder cattle setting contract highs, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.125 cent per lb lower to 0.225 higher with only February off at 65.600 cents. Distant December and February posted new contract highs.
Feeder cattle futures ended up 0.275 to 0.050 lower with March up most at 68.975 cents per lb. January posted a new contract high of 69.125 cents.

Trading was thin in live cattle futures as the market awaited fresh input from cash cattle markets next week. Forecasts for improving weather and this week's slipping beef values weighed on futures while underlying support persisted because of feedlots' very current marketing conditions and light weights on cattle going to market, they said.

Trading may be mixed again next week, buffeted by expectations for the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report to be released next Friday and another holiday-shortened session on Monday in observance of Martin Luther King, they said.
Early analysts' estimates on the report pointed to on-feed supplies at between 102 and 105 percent of a year ago.
Early trade placement estimates were running at 103 to 112 percent of a year ago and marketing estimates at 99 to 107.1 percent of last year.

Trading was also light in live cattle options with commercials buying April 70 calls and commission house selling February 68 calls. Spreading in April, buying of 68 calls and selling of 64 puts also was noted, pit sources said.

Profit taking weighed on feeder cattle futures early, but losses were pared by midsession and futures moved up late to set a new contract high in January on support from lower corn futures, a higher CME feeder cattle index and expected tighter feeder cattle supplies by next fall, traders said.
Expectations are that recent harsh weather in major cow/calf-areas likely will reduce calf production this spring and in turn, cut feeder cattle supplies by next fall, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.03 at $68.56 per cwt, the highest level since March 20, 1995.
Futures closed early at 1200 CST/1800 GMT ahead of the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday on Monday. Markets will also close early Monday in observance of the holiday.
